## Does Abortion Increase Breast Cancer Risk? The Evidence Says No

The claim that abortion increases breast cancer risk is **not supported by the scientific consensus**, despite its persistence in some advocacy circles.

**What major scientific bodies conclude:** The National Cancer Institute convened a 2003 workshop of over 100 leading experts who reviewed population-based, clinical, and animal studies on pregnancy and breast cancer risk ([cancer.gov](https://www.cancer.gov/types/breast/abortion-miscarriage-risk)). More recently, a 2018 report from the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine—reviewing the safety of abortion in the U.S.—also concluded abortion does not raise breast cancer risk ([cancer.org](https://www.cancer.org/cancer/risk-prevention/medical-treatments/abortion-and-breast-cancer-risk.html)). The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists and Susan G. Komen concur that higher-quality research finds no link ([komen.org](https://www.komen.org/breast-cancer/facts-statistics/research-studies/topics/abortion-and-breast-cancer-risk/)).

**Why some older studies suggested a link:** Early evidence came primarily from case-control studies, which asked women to recall their reproductive histories after already being diagnosed with cancer (or not). This design is vulnerable to **recall/reporting bias**—women with breast cancer may be more forthcoming about a past abortion than healthy control subjects, since they have a stronger motivation to search for a possible cause. Cancer.org's archived methodological review notes: "Early studies... were methodologically flawed... Case-control studies, which are prone to recall bias, pointed to a slight increase in risk" ([web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20110629014841/http://www.cancer.org/Cancer/BreastCancer/MoreInformation/is-abortion-linked-to-breast-cancer)). Larger, more rigorous prospective studies and registry-based record-linkage studies, which avoid self-reporting bias entirely, have not found this association.

**Bottom line:** The claim is a well-documented pseudoscience narrative rooted in older, bias-prone studies. Current consensus among major health and scientific institutions is that abortion does not increase breast cancer risk.
